schema_version: v0 — component-charter shape; migrates into the intention envelope when MAP.md Q6 lands
what: STAGE 7 OF THE CHART CHAIN, and a machine of its own since 2026-08-13. It answers ONE narrow question — what does DONE mean, measured? — and emits the smallest typed artifact that fully determines what the next stage needs. The chain's last leg and the one that opens the BUILDME door: its berth is what /sail requires, so 'done' is settled BEFORE the build rather than argued after it. Three strata, cheapest first: FLOOR (deterministic, this module), TREE (this nexus's own corpus through cairn/tools/tree), CEILING (the skill's assembly). The exit artifact berths in instance-space and the deposit-back lands it as the tree's memory of this class of request.
why: Akien, verbatim 2026-08-13: "orient is a machine. the other pre-build steps are each their own machine." A machine is tools plus the glue that holds them together, and that is exactly the shape here: cairn/tools/chain's grammar plus this stage's own question. THE LIVED SYMPTOM the whole chain answers is a build that starts before anyone settled what was being built — the web-server carrier miss, bounds-checking that never ran to completion. A stage that is its own machine can be fired, proved, and replaced alone; one that is a function in a 1,300-line module cannot. WHY THE RECORD AND NOT A COMPLAINT LIST (Akien, 2026-08-13): "passing such a thing without inspecting it means passing a mystery if something downstream fails … if every machine and even some more complex tools have their own inspector and gate, then each has documented and controllable quality validation … we can backtrack and see exactly where something went awry even if it's not something we're specifically looking for yet." A complaint list is empty both when every check passed and when no check ran, so the stage downstream is handed a mystery in exactly the case he named. The entries that PASSED are the ones nobody was looking for. "We might have to add more or better inspection questions, but that's fine. we learn as we go" — so the question list grows, and every addition is one more entry a reader sees whether it passed or failed.

feedback.why: MEASURED LINK: inspect_validate opens on hypothesize_ref (validate.py:152), and the packet's own claimed_pieces are read straight out of that berth's hypotheses (validate.py:122). Akien's rule for the -2- edge, 2026-08-14, verbatim: "the purpose of an inspector/gate combination is to qa THE OUTPUT OF THE THING BEFORE IT THATS COMING IN AS ITS INPUT. IF IT FAILS, GENERALLY THAT FEEDBACK GOES BACK TO THE UPSTREAM CREATIVE ENTITY. In some cases it skips levels." REFINED BY HIM THE SAME DAY, and the refinement is what `to` MEANS: "really it shouldn't be 'number of steps' it should be 'to the feedback target' which is likely to be the previous step." So this field is not a hop count and never was — it names the TARGET. The previous step is the common case, not the definition, and a route that lands elsewhere is not a special case needing a count. Validate's question is what would prove or falsify each hypothesis, so a criterion with no instrument is nearly always a hypothesis stated in terms nothing can measure — which under Law 3 is the defect being caught one stage downstream of where it was authored. Hypothesize can restate it; validate can only refuse it. The one-address shape cannot split a segment's findings by which side of its door they indict; see cairn/tools/feedback filed edge (e).

invoke: fired by the skill that runs the chain; the writer door is write_validate; the inspector is inspect_validate(packet) and returns the proof record without taking a verdict, so a caller can READ what this stage proved without provoking its refusal
entry: Carved out of the chart machine on 2026-08-13 under Akien's ruling — "chart is a skill, it calls a collection of machines. that's the intention." The chart charter it was carved from is the design record of the whole chain and now berths with the skill at cairn/skills/chart/intention+why.json; this file holds only what is THIS component's. THE RESIDUE, RECORDED RATHER THAN PAPERED OVER: the judge ROSTER is not declared anywhere. `installed_judges_find_nothing` names, in its ACTUAL, which judges FIRED — it cannot name which judges PASSED, because judge_* returns findings and not attendance. So for the judge half of this stage the record is still a complaint list, and it is one for the exact reason the ruling names: a silent judge and an absent judge read the same. This is measured, not assumed — read judge_* in this module. Closing it wants attendance emitted BY the judge and a roster the entry can compare its ACTUAL against — filed as ticket a-judge-declares-its-attendance, not left as prose. Until it lands, the falsifier clause above holds only over the SHAPE half of this stage's record.
state_and_history: state.json + history.json beside this charter. Both were born at the carve-out: the voyages that built this stage are recorded in the chart machine's history, which stays whole with the skill — a record of truth is never split (Law 7).
gates: THE STAGE'S OWN INSPECTOR AND ITS OWN GATE, at this address (ruling 2026-08-13 every-machine-carries-its-own-inspector-and-gate). ``inspect_validate`` returns a PROOF RECORD — one entry per check that ran, EXPECTED beside ACTUAL, passes included — and ``validate_validate`` is the == compare over it, per entry, with no oracle anywhere near it. The shared half of the record comes from cairn/tools/chain's ``common_shape_record`` so the eight doors cannot drift apart; the stage-specific half is written here. Refusals still name every shape lack at once (ticket chart-doors-refuse-in-one-pass), and they are DERIVED from the record's mismatches, so the gate and the sentence it prints cannot disagree about what failed. A CHECK THAT DID NOT RUN IS ABSENT, NOT PASSED: guarded checks make the record SHORTER, never cleaner.
falsifier: RED on any of: (1) this stage reading its input from anywhere but the previous stage's BERTHED packet; (2) a door that dribbles refusals instead of naming every lack in one pass; (3) a packet admitted whose provenance does not cover every authored field; (4) this module importing a sibling stage — the legs speak the grammar, never each other. (5) a check in this stage's inspector that PASSES SILENTLY — every check that ran appears in the record with its EXPECTED beside its ACTUAL, and a check that could not run is ABSENT rather than passed, so a check that stops running makes the record SHORTER and never cleaner; (6) a refusal sentence assembled from anywhere but the record's own mismatches — the gate and the sentence it prints cannot be allowed to disagree about what failed; (7) an oracle consulted anywhere on this path, at fire time or at sleep — `bin/cmd/determinism` must keep reading this component PURE DETERMINISTIC and REFUSES GATE.
horizon: re-read when the chain's stage list changes, or when this stage's tree stratum goes live against a real embed seam.
how_it_learns: the deposit-back: every ceiling assembly deposits its own answer into this nexus's tree, so the next similar request walks to a settled answer instead of re-deriving it (Law 1 as runtime). The dial (cairn/skills/chart/dial.py) is the instrument that says whether the floor+tree fraction is actually growing — a nexus that never compiles is a ceiling doing the floor's job forever.

Law 4 (the door is physics, not a habit of asking)
